terms.meaning: a named value such as a colour, font or size, defined once and reused
a colour written as a code such as a hash followed by six characters
text that grows smoothly with the screen width
digits that are all the same width so numbers line up in columns

depends_on: Font package imported in src/app/layout.tsx (named in the file)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Header and design rules
sections.what: Comment block that names this file as the single home for raw colours and sets the rule against pure black or pure red. Yellow is reserved for decisions and grades.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the look consistent and makes the yellow highlight rare.
sections.watch_out: The rules are not enforced by code, so raw colours added elsewhere would break them.

sections.name: :root
sections.title: Light colours and named meanings
sections.what: Defines the palette, then named meanings such as background, text, line and focus, plus the font families and corner sizes used in light mode.
sections.why: Likely reason: named meanings let the theme change without editing each component.
sections.watch_out: Font names rely on a font package loaded at startup. Without it, fallback fonts show.

sections.name: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)
sections.title: Dark theme from system setting
sections.what: When the device is set to dark, applies dark values for most colours, unless the page is forced to light with the data-theme attribute.
sections.why: Likely reason: follows the user's system preference automatically.
sections.watch_out: Its values repeat the explicit dark block, so the two must be kept matched.

sections.name: :root[data-theme="dark"]
sections.title: Dark theme set explicitly
sections.what: Applies the same dark values when the page is set to dark with the data-theme attribute, whatever the system setting.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a user pick dark mode inside the app, overriding the system setting.
sections.watch_out: It nearly duplicates the system dark block, so a value changed in one but not the other will look different depending on the setting.

sections.name: :root
sections.title: Text sizes and number styling
sections.what: Defines six fluid text sizes that grow smoothly with screen width, a class that lines up numbers in columns, and two font helper classes.
sections.why: Likely reason: a consistent type scale that works on phones and desktops.
sections.watch_out: Numbers align only when they carry the tabular class, so an unmarked number will not line up.

summary: The one place where the app's raw colours, fonts, corner sizes and text sizes are defined, in light and dark versions.
purpose: Gives every stylesheet and image maker the same named values.
why: The header says it is the only place raw colour values live, following the design document named there.
how: Defines the palette, then meaning-based names that point to it. Light values sit in the main block. Dark values apply by system setting or by an explicit dark attribute. Text size steps and number alignment are at the end.
inputs: None. It is read by stylesheets and by tokenValues.ts.
outputs: CSS variables for other styles to use.
risks: Dark values are repeated in two places, so one can be changed without the other. Fonts show only when the font package is loaded.
debug: If a colour is wrong, find its name here and check which block applies. If dark mode differs from the system, check the data-theme attribute.
